title: From EBIC to Scanning Transmission EBIC: Probing Functional Oxide-Based Two Terminal Lamella Devices
content: Electron beam-induced current (EBIC) has proven invaluable for mapping recombination sites, measuring carrier transport properties such as diffusion length, determining junction depths, and indentifying inversion layers in semiconductors [1, 2]. While EBIC has traditionally been applied to bulk specimens, there is growing interest in extending its use to cross-sectional lamellae for more localized device analysis [3].
